chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn al-Husayn narrated to us from Sa'd ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata from Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him). He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying:

O assembly of the Muhajirun and Ansar! Shall I not guide you to that by which, if you hold firmly to it, you will never go astray after me? They said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: This Ali is my brother, my legatee, my vizier, my inheritor, my vicegerent, and your Imam. So love him for the sake of love for me, and honour him for the sake of my honour, for indeed Gabriel commanded me to say this to you.

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam — the divinely guided leader of the community; the highest title of authority in Shia theology
key_terms.خَلِيفَة: Vicegerent/caliph — the designated successor and ruler; here specifically applied to Ali as the Prophet's successor
key_terms.مَعْشَر: Assembly/company — used for a gathered group being addressed; carries a sense of formal, collective address
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Legatee/executor — one designated to carry out the Prophet's will and continue his mission; a key term in Shia doctrine of succession

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Ali's role as Imam to the Muhajirun and Ansar?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) gathers the Muhajirun and Ansar and publicly designates Ali ibn Abi Talib as his brother, legatee, vizier, inheritor, vicegerent, and Imam — the one to whom all must hold for guidance after his passing. This hadith, transmitted through the revered companion Salman al-Farisi and reaching al-Saduq through a chain including the historian al-Thaqafi, presents one of the clearest formulations of the doctrine of Ali's appointed leadership. The Prophet's invocation of Gabriel's command underscores the divine origin of this designation, framing it not as a personal preference but as a divine decree.
